newsitem.title: ITALY: Enel, Deutsche Telekom bid for cellphone licence.
newsitem.headline: Enel, Deutsche Telekom bid for cellphone licence.

text.p: Italian electricity utility Enel is to launch a joint bid with Germany's Deutsche Telekom for Italy's third mobile phone operating licence, the Treasury said in a statement on Friday.
Enel would take a 51 percent controlling stake in the new venture, to have a start-up capital of 200 billion lire, with Deutsche Telekom holding the remaining 49 percent.
Telecommunications Minister Antonio Maccanico was reported in Italian newspaper Corriere della Sera as saying that the government would invite bids for the licence next month.
The statement said Enel intended to sell its entire stake in the joint venture in the medium term. Deutsche would have the option of selling part of its stake.
The Italian mobile phone market is currently dominated by Telecom Italia Mobile, controlled by state telecom holding company Stet.
A second operator, Omnitel Pronto Italia, in which information technology group Olivetti has a dominant stake, started operation in 1996.
